correctness.rationale: The upper bound is proved for n>=4 by counting heavy-coordinate incidences: every word has >=1 heavy coordinate, precisely 12 words have exactly 1, all others contribute >=2, and each of three pure receive lists has <=L parents; hence 2M-12<=3L. For L>=6, all 12 one-heavy words plus floor((L-4)/2), ceil((L-4)/2), floor((L-4)/2) balanced edge words have exactly floor(3L/2)+6 distinct words and each of six trace lists obeys capacity L when n>=ceil(L/2)+1. For L=5, the explicit 13-of-15 length-four code covers all six omitted-parent traces and has an injective, signature-preserving lift to every larger n. For even L, equality forces inclusion of all 12 one-heavy words and exactly two heavy coordinates for every remaining word with each pure load L. All critical inequalities, parity boundaries and L=5 exception have been reconstructed. Standard-library checks ran on 198 constructive parameter cases and exhaustively enumerated all 32768 subcodes at n=4. Finite checking alone is not used as proof.

originality.rationale: The January primary theorem on two survivors assumes unique decoding and gives q+I(q,n), which equals three for q=3,n>=4; its pairwise-disjointness proof does not imply bounded-list capacity. The March primary work treats metric-ball counts and unique-decoding packing/GV bounds, not the six-output list-incidence maximum. Previous accessible results with exactly the same channel cover only L=4, while another covers 2<=L<=k and thus L<=2 at k=2. The new infinite high-list law for every L>=5, including the 3L/2 slope and even-L equality condition, is neither a restatement nor an implication of those results. Searches did not expose a stronger result; unindexed equivalent work remains a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed publication or equivalent nonstandard formulation may contain the same infinite high-list capacity law.

value.rationale: List decoding of unordered survivors is a motivated extension of the established multiset deletion model with genuinely different incidence geometry from unique decoding. The theorem supplies an exact infinite two-parameter capacity (not just a lower bound), an explicit all-parameter family of attaining codes, a 3/2 asymptotic list-capacity slope, and necessary optimizer rigidity for every even L; it includes arbitrarily large list sizes and source lengths. The twelve exceptional one-heavy source words and three-edge balancing mechanism explain the capacity. The uniform sufficient threshold is not claimed sharp. This natural exact invariant remains useful even without a general q-ary extension.
